title: From n-gram to Attention: How Model Architectures Learn and Propagate Bias in Language Modeling
benchmark_measurement: Stereotype detection in religious contexts, measured by comparing the log-likelihood of stereotypical vs. anti-stereotypical sentence pairs.
findings: Religion, along with gender and physical appearance, was found to be a 'medium amplification' bias category, meaning it was more significantly amplified by the models compared to low-tier categories like age or disability, but less so than high-tier categories like sexual orientation.
